'''Hartmuth Christian Kolb''' (born 10 August 1964){{citation needed|date=December 2022|reason=None of the existing citations his date of birth or early life.}} is a [[German chemist]]. He is considered one of the founders of [[click chemistry]].<ref name=KFS2001>{{Cite journal|last1=Kolb|first1=Hartmuth C.|last2=Finn|first2=M. G.|last3=Sharpless|first3=K. Barry|date=1 June 2001|title=Click Chemistry: Diverse Chemical Function from a Few Good Reactions|journal=[[Angewandte Chemie]]|volume=40|issue=11|pages=2004–2021|issn=1521-3773|pmid=11433435|doi=10.1002/1521-3773(20010601)40:11<2004::AID-ANIE2004>3.0.CO;2-5|doi-access=}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
After graduating from high school in Marsberg in 1983, Kolb studied at the [[University of Hanover]] under the direction of Professor H.M.R. Hoffmann.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kolb |first=Hartmuth C. |date=1990 |title=A ring contraction of 6-alkoxy-2,3-dihydro-6h-pyran-3-ones to polyfunctionalized cyclopentenones |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0040402001878200 |journal=Tetrahedron |volume=46 |issue=15 |pages=5127–5144 |via=Elsevier Science Direct |doi=10.1016/S0040-4020(01)87820-0|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He received his doctorate in 1991 as an academic student of [[Steven V. Ley|Steven Ley]] at [[Imperial College London]] with a thesis on preparative [[organic chemistry]] (''Synthesis of the decalin fragment of [[azadirachtin]]''). As a postdoctoral fellow he worked with [[Karl Barry Sharpless|Barry Sharpless]] at the [[Scripps Research Institute]] in [[La Jolla|La Jolla, California]].

== Career ==
He then worked in the research department of [[Ciba-Geigy]] in [[Basel]] from 1993 to 1997 before taking up a managerial position at [[Coelacanth Corporation]], founded by Sharpless and A. Bader in [[Princeton, New Jersey]]. Coelacanth was eventually acquired by [[Lexicon Pharmaceuticals]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lexicon Genetics to Acquire Coelacanth Corporation {{!}} Lexicon Pharmaceuticals, Inc. |url=https://www.lexpharma.com/media-center/news/289-2001-06-13%2014-56-55 |access-date=2022-10-08 |website=www.lexpharma.com |archive-date=8 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221008151828/https://www.lexpharma.com/media-center/news/289-2001-06-13%2014-56-55 }}</ref>

In 2002, Kolb obtained an associate professorship in the Department of Chemistry at the [[Scripps Research Institute]]. Kolb later obtained a professorship at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]].

In 2004 Kolb returned to industry and became Vice President of Molecular Imaging [[Biomarker]] Research at [[Siemens Healthcare]] in [[Culver City, California]]. In 2013, Siemens sold two of the Positron Emission Tomography (PET) radiotracers developed there to Eli Lilly and Company, most notably the Tau PET tracer [18F]-T807 (aka AV1451, Flortaucipir, Tauvid), now FDA approved for PET imaging of the brain to estimate the density and distribution of aggregated tau neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs) in adult patients with cognitive impairment who are being evaluated for Alzheimer's disease (AD).<ref>{{Cite web |title=TAUVID™ (flortaucipir F 18 injection), for intravenous use. Initial U.S. Approval: 2020 |url=https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/212123s000lbl.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200720035819/https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2020/212123s000lbl.pdf|archive-date=20 July 2020}}</ref> Simultaneously, Kolb joined [[Avid Radiopharmaceuticals]] in [[Philadelphia]], Pennsylvania, a subsidiary of [[Eli Lilly and Company]], as vice president of research, and later Janssen Research & Development (Johnson & Johnson) as vice president of Neuroscience Biomarkers & Global Imaging. 

After leaving Johnson & Johnson in 2024, he joined Enigma Biomedical Group as their Chief Scientific Officer to focus on the development of CNS imaging tracers. He is also Visiting Professor at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].

== Work ==
Together with [[Karl Barry Sharpless|Barry Sharpless]] and [[M.G. Finn]], Kolb developed the concept of [[click chemistry]], an approach to simplify synthesis by focusing on a few chemical reactions that are similar in nature.<ref name=KFS2001></ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Finn |first1=M. G. |last2=Kolb |first2=Hartmuth C. |last3=Sharpless |first3=K. Barry |date=12 January 2022 |title=Click chemistry connections for functional discovery |journal=[[Nature Synthesis]] |language=en |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=8–10 |doi=10.1038/s44160-021-00017-w |bibcode=2022NatSy...1....8F |s2cid=245916585 |issn=2731-0582|doi-access=free }}</ref> The associated scientific publication Click chemistry: diverse chemical function from a few good reactions has been cited more than 20,000 times (as of 2025) and was the foundation for the [[2022 Nobel Prize laureates|2022 Nobel Prize]] in Chemistry for K. Barry Sharpless, [[Carolyn Bertozzi]] and [[Morten Meldal]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scientific Background on the Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2022 |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2022/10/advanced-chemistryprize2022.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Click Chemistry: The Certainty of Chance |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2025/02/sharpless-lecture.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sharpless |first1=K. Barry |last2=Finn |first2=M. G. |last3=Kolb |first3=Hartmuth C. |title=Click Chemistry: The Certainty of Chance (Nobel Lecture)** |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |date=11 April 2025 |volume=64 |issue=16 |article-number=e202501229 |doi=10.1002/anie.202501229 |pmid=40109146 |bibcode=2025ACIE...6401229S }}</ref> Kolb refined the method by combining it as in-situ click chemistry with [[Microfluidics|microfluidic]] processes. This makes it particularly easy to synthesize new inhibitors for various [[enzyme]]s. 
[[File:2022 Nobel awards ceremony.jpg|alt=K. Barry Sharpless with collaborators Hartmuth Kolb and M.G. Finn at the 2022 Nobel awards ceremony.|thumb|[[K. Barry Sharpless]] (center) with collaborators Hartmuth Kolb (right) and [[M.G. Finn]] (left) at the 2022 Nobel awards ceremony.]]

Kolb's more recent work deals with the synthesis of new tracers for [[positron emission tomography]] (e.g. for detecting the [[tau protein]] in [[Alzheimer's disease]]) and with the clinical testing of these tracers, a key highlight being [18F]-T807,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Xia |first1=Chun-Fang |last2=Arteaga |first2=Janna |last3=Chen |first3=Gang |last4=Gangadharmath |first4=Umesh |last5=Gomez |first5=Luis F. |last6=Kasi |first6=Dhanalakshmi |last7=Lam |first7=Chung |last8=Liang |first8=Qianwa |last9=Liu |first9=Changhui |last10=Mocharla |first10=Vani P. |last11=Mu |first11=Fanrong |last12=Sinha |first12=Anjana |last13=Su |first13=Helen |last14=Szardenings |first14=A. Katrin |last15=Walsh |first15=Joseph C. |date=November 2013 |title=[ 18 F]T807, a novel tau positron emission tomography imaging agent for Alzheimer's disease |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1016/j.jalz.2012.11.008 |journal=Alzheimer's & Dementia |language=en |volume=9 |issue=6 |pages=666–676 |doi=10.1016/j.jalz.2012.11.008 |pmid=23411393 |s2cid=1079628 |issn=1552-5260|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Chien |first1=David T. |last2=Bahri |first2=Shadfar |last3=Szardenings |first3=A. Katrin |last4=Walsh |first4=Joseph C. |last5=Mu |first5=Fanrong |last6=Su |first6=Min-Ying |last7=Shankle |first7=William R. |last8=Elizarov |first8=Arkadij |last9=Kolb |first9=Hartmuth C. |date=20 June 2013 |title=Early Clinical PET Imaging Results with the Novel PHF-Tau Radioligand [F-18]-T807 |url=https://www.medra.org/servlet/aliasResolver?alias=iospress&doi=10.3233/JAD-122059 |journal=Journal of Alzheimer's Disease |volume=34 |issue=2 |pages=457–468 |doi=10.3233/JAD-122059|pmid=23234879 |s2cid=46044539 }}</ref> also known as AV1451, [[Flortaucipir (18F)|Flortaucipir]], Tauvid, which was approved in 2020 by the US food and drug administration (FDA) for imaging [[neurofibrillary tangle]]s in adults who are being evaluated for Alzheimer's Disease.

Kolb's lab has developed a blood plasma assay for phospho-217-Tau (p217Tau), which shows potential as a highly accurate peripheral biomarker for [[amyloid]] and Tau status in Alzheimer's Disease.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Triana-Baltzer |first1=Gallen |last2=Moughadam |first2=Setareh |last3=Slemmon |first3=Randy |last4=Van Kolen |first4=Kristof |last5=Theunis |first5=Clara |last6=Mercken |first6=Marc |last7=Kolb |first7=Hartmuth C. |date=January 2021 |title=Development and validation of a high-sensitivity assay for measuring p217+tau in plasma |journal= Alzheimer's & Dementia: Diagnosis, Assessment & Disease Monitoring|language=en |volume=13 |issue=1 |article-number=e12204 |doi=10.1002/dad2.12204 |doi-access=free |issn=2352-8729 |pmc=8158165 |pmid=34095436}}</ref>

==Awards==
Kolb was chosen as the recipient of the 2015 Alzheimer Award by the [[Journal of Alzheimer's Disease]]<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.iospress.com/news/hartmuth-kolb-phd-wins-2015-alzheimer-award |title=Hartmuth Kolb, PhD, Wins 2015 Alzheimer Award |date=26 June 2015 |work=[[IOS Press]]}}</ref> and he was one of the recipients of the Royal Society of Chemistry 2021 Organic Division Horizon Prize: Robert Robinson Award in Synthetic Organic Chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Multidimensional Click Chemistry {{!}} 2021 Organic Division Horizon Prize: Robert Robinson Award in Synthetic Organic Chemistry winner |url=https://www.rsc.org/prizes-funding/prizes/2021-winners/multidimensional-click-chemistry-team/ |access-date=2022-10-08 |website=Royal Society of Chemistry |language=en-GB}}</ref>
